findings: SearchParams defaults maxMatches=5, filterSelf=true, filterGroups=true and maxThresh=0. Thus full active VP-tree recall from v1 does not imply an unlimited application result set. Database::searchIndex sorts then stops when admitted valid group reaches maxMatches.

searchIndex looks up each match and appends only if media.isValid(), otherwise warns stale/corrupt. mediaWithId returns default Media unless exactly one SQL row exists. A zero-ID tree tombstone therefore does not by itself prove a bogus user-visible file: validity and DB contents are caller gates; default Media internals still unread.

Adaptive widening checks raw matches.count() <= minMatches before self/invalid filtering and before maxMatches capping. Raw match count is not necessarily usable distinct results. maxThresh widening is disabled by default, so no default widening failure claimed.

SearchParams explicitly says only Engine::query incorporates all parameters. Database::similarTo handles subset slicing and per-group filtering; Engine and full group postprocessing remain unread. Do not attribute index-level controls to full product recall or grouping.

Generic index tests require external TEST_DATA_DIR, remove/recreate its _index directory, run actual scanner/database and require at least40 groups for a40x5 corpus. They require group.count()>1 rather than all expected five identities, so test names/comments do not establish exhaustive neighborhood recall. Tests were only read; no external corpus or directories touched.

Base add/remove tests check three queried identities disappear and re-add produces comparable groups. They do not test top-k completeness, all threshold boundaries, or raw-to-valid widening. The prior independent seeded VP controls cover a different narrower layer.
